feedback.problem: Find the maximum value of $Q(x)=2{x}_{1}^{2}-7{x}_{2}^{2}+4{x}_{3}^{2}$ given that $‖x‖=1.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, notice that ${x}_{1}^{2}\ge 0$ and ${x}_{2}^{2}\ge 0.$ So, we have that

$$
2{x}_{1}^{2}\le 4{x}_{1}^{2},\,-7{x}_{2}^{2}\le 4{x}_{2}^{2}.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =2{x}_{1}^{2}-7{x}_{2}^{2}+4{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & \le 4{x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{2}^{2}+4{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & =4({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall that $‖x‖=1$ is equivalent to ${x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}=1.$ So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}4({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2})=4(1)=4.\end{aligned}
$$

and, in turn, $Q(x)\le 4.$

So, the value of $Q(x)$ can be no greater than $4.$ But before we conclude that $4$ is the maximum, we need to find a vector such that $Q(x)=4.$

Notice that when $x={[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{T},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =2{x}_{1}^{2}-7{x}_{2}^{2}+4{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & =2(0)^{2}-7(0)^{2}+4(1)^{2} \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, given that $‖x‖=1,$ the maximum value of $Q(x)$ is equal to $4.$
